data.name: Artifact Adventure
data.detailed_description:
The ultimate mix of classic aesthetics and modern open world RPG!

Welcome to a truly open world RPG. Travel the world in the way you want, taking on the challenges you deem worthy of your time. Travel by blimp, artifact or by foot, and discover a vast world rich with characters, civilizations, monsters and adventure.
Take on quests the way you want to. Every quest has multiple ways to complete it, and the choices you make always have repercussions. Will you save the girl about to be sacrificed to the village fire god, or will you let her burn because it's not worth your time?

No matter what decision you make, there are always consequences. Your adventure begins with 1 of 3 choices that drastically change the flow of the entire game:
  • Freely fly around the world. (Airship)
  • Receive a special power. (Artifact)
  • Unlock the mysteries of the world. (Key of Time)
Everything you do determines which of over 70 endings you will get.
This is the truly the perfect definition of an open-world adventure... an Artifact Adventure!

THE CLASSES OF ARTIFACT ADVENTURE

Choose from 6 different classes and form a 4 character party for your adventure!

THE WARRIOR
Considered the cornerstone of any team, the warrior has high HP and Defense, and is able to wear heavy armor. Their stats make them perfect for new players.

THE HERMIT
Skilled with a bow and armed with extensive medical knowledge, the hermit is also the fastest class among the six classes available.

THE SHAMAN
Possessing more intelligence and MP than any other class, the Shaman makes for a powerful magical ally. They're also capable of casting unusual spells with their staves.

THE MONK
Skilled in the martial arts, the Monk is a perfect choice for dealing quick damage to enemies. They also have a chance of attacking twice in a single turn when fighting bare-fisted.

THE DREAMER
Able to fight using their dreams and equip any armor in the game, the Dreamer is capable of doing everything...and nothing.

THE EXPLORER
Blessed with both strong attacks and high intelligence, the Explorer is a hybrid class known for wielding a very special gun.

data.short_description: The horribly toxic Swamp King has risen once again! Gather your party and set out on an open world, retro-styled, RPG adventure. Powerful mystical artifacts are scattered about the world, each able to grant you new powers. Which will you choose? What is your destiny?

reviews.review:
Artifact Adventure is a retro-styled role-playing game built around exploration, meaningful choices, and the freedom to shape a journey instead of simply following a rigid storyline. Developed by bluffman and published by PLAYISM, it deliberately recalls the appearance and mechanics of early Japanese RPGs with its pixel graphics, turn-based battles, compact character classes, and straightforward interface. Beneath that nostalgic exterior, however, is a surprisingly flexible adventure that places considerable importance on where the player travels, which situations they become involved in, and how they resolve the problems encountered along the way.

The story takes place in a fantasy world facing the threat of the Swamp King, but the game does not constantly force the player toward the next major objective. Exploration is a central part of the experience, with towns, characters, quests, enemies, and secrets scattered throughout the world. This freedom makes wandering worthwhile because discovering a location can lead to an unexpected event rather than merely another combat encounter. Players who enjoy searching every corner of an RPG map are rewarded more generously than those who simply want to move directly from one story objective to another.

One of the game's defining ideas appears near the beginning, when the player must make an important choice between valuable advantages. Options such as an airship, a powerful artifact, or the Key of Time encourage distinctly different approaches to the adventure. Mobility can make exploring the world considerably more convenient, while other choices emphasize abilities or access to mysteries. Because the player cannot simply begin with everything, this decision immediately introduces the concept that gaining one opportunity may mean giving up another. It also gives repeat playthroughs a stronger purpose.

Quest design expands upon this philosophy by allowing decisions to influence later outcomes. The player is frequently given room to decide whether to intervene in situations and how particular problems should be handled. Instead of treating every quest as a checklist with one correct conclusion, Artifact Adventure makes the player's actions part of the story. Its large collection of possible ending variations reflects the accumulated consequences of these choices. Not every ending represents a completely different final chapter, but the system still provides an entertaining sense that individual decisions leave a mark on the world.

Party construction offers another source of flexibility. Players assemble a four-character group using six available classes, including the Warrior, Hermit, Shaman, Monk, Dreamer, and Explorer. Familiar archetypes make the system accessible, with the Warrior serving as a durable physical combatant and the Shaman providing magical strength. The Hermit mixes ranged capabilities with useful support functions, while the Monk favors speed and physical offense. More unusual options such as the Dreamer and Explorer provide additional possibilities for players interested in less conventional party combinations.

Combat remains firmly rooted in traditional turn-based RPG design. Battles revolve around selecting actions, exploiting the strengths of individual party members, managing resources, and gradually improving the group's effectiveness. The system is not overloaded with modern layers of mechanics, which makes it easy to understand but can also leave encounters feeling comparatively simple for players accustomed to more elaborate contemporary RPG combat. Much of the strategic enjoyment comes from creating an effective party and learning how different classes complement one another rather than mastering an exceptionally complex battle engine.

The visual presentation is intentionally modest. Pixel artwork and simple environments evoke the era of classic console RPGs, while the interface favors function over spectacle. This approach gives the game a consistent identity, although it also means that players expecting detailed animations, cinematic storytelling, extensive visual effects, or lavish production values may find the presentation sparse. Its charm depends heavily on whether the player appreciates minimalist retro design. Imagination fills in many of the details that a modern RPG would normally present through elaborate graphics and cinematics.

Where the experience becomes particularly rewarding is replayability. Different opening decisions, alternative quest resolutions, multiple party configurations, exploration choices, and numerous ending outcomes make it difficult to experience everything in a single journey. A second playthrough can therefore be approached as more than simply repeating the same campaign. Choosing another initial advantage or building a substantially different party can alter the rhythm of exploration, while making different decisions reveals consequences that were previously unavailable.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unsupported. Players primarily interested in experiencing it on Valve's handheld should keep this limitation in mind rather than assuming that the simple controls automatically guarantee full compatibility. Its design may appear ideal for portable play, but the official Deck classification does not currently provide that assurance.

Overall, Artifact Adventure is most successful when treated as a compact tribute to classic RPG design that gives players considerably more agency than its simple appearance suggests. Its combat and graphics are deliberately old-fashioned, but its open exploration, consequential decisions, party customization, and extensive outcome system create an adventure with genuine replay potential. It will appeal most strongly to players who value discovery and choice over cinematic presentation, while those seeking sophisticated modern combat or high-end visuals may find it overly restrained. The combination of nostalgic mechanics and nonlinear progression nevertheless gives it an identity that extends beyond being a simple retro imitation.

Rating: 7/10
